analysis: Reviewed EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift (base 540-992, head 1-535). The security-relevant change is small: submitTokenized (both overloads) gains an optional per-request `stopStringScope` parameter (head lines 61, 80, 129-131), and the translation call at head 255-259 passes nil when ownedEngine is CBv2NativeBlockEngine, otherwise `stopStringScope ?? self.stopStringScope`. The base used the bridge-level scope only. The change affects only how stop strings are matched on generated output. It does not touch cache scope (cacheScope/checkpointScope derivation, head 263 and 347-380), cache salt, SSD staging, shared KV reservation, deadline checks, retirement transfer, or encryption. The T-041 cache-isolation properties (coordinator-authored cacheScope, HMAC lookup tags, per-request receipt IDs) are unchanged in the visible code. The base-side unit (540-992) is in an unchanged region, apart from the base line 250 change. It also shows the pre-submit release, retirement and pump-ownership paths, which are unchanged. The change at head 948 (onTermination) was not visible in the truncated head text, since head text ends at line 535, so I could not inspect the changed head region at the file tail. Open integration questions: (1) the callers that now supply `stopStringScope` are in other files and were not supplied, so whether it can be influenced by a consumer is unverified; a consumer-controlled scope could alter output truncation, but that is not an exposure of prompts. (2) Dropping the scope for the native block engine changes stop matching semantics. This is a correctness effect, not a confidentiality or authorization one. No concrete regression is identified in the supplied evidence.
